brief: Goldman's Duttenhoefer's Daily (24 Sep 2026). September's PMI beat (57.0 vs 53.7 consensus, fastest expansion since 2021) combined with hawkish Fed comments pushed the US 10yr to 5.11% and raised market-implied odds of an October hike to 70%. The S&P fell 75bps, framed as "good macro news is bad news for markets." GS revised its own Fed call to match: it now expects a second 25bp hike in October, changed from its prior single-September-hike view, reasoning that FOMC language on a "timelier return" to the 2% target supports back-to-back hikes. Moody's warns selective credit markets are squeezing lower-rated borrowers, with the 2028-29 maturity wall likely to drive more liability-management exercises and distressed exchanges. Pandemic-era fixed-rate debt has held corporate net interest payments to 0.4% of GDP even as federal net interest costs climbed to 3.6%, a gap GS expects to close as corporate debt refinances higher. On earnings, GS's base case is deceleration, not collapse, despite some over-earning: EPS growth of 11% is forecast for 2027 ($415) and 2028 ($460), as a fading AI-investment tailwind transitions into an AI-productivity boost. Also covered: Alibaba's AI chips as a Nvidia substitute, Meta's Muse app (500k users), and AAII sentiment at 2026 lows.
